what_its_for: Retapamulin is an antibiotic ointment used to treat small infected skin wounds, such as impetigo (a common skin infection that causes red sores or blisters). It works by killing certain bacteria on your skin.
how_to_take: Wash your hands before and after using this medicine. Apply a thin layer of the ointment to the infected area of skin twice a day. You may cover the treated area with a clean bandage or gauze if needed. Do not put this ointment in your eyes, nose, mouth, or on your lips. It is for use on the skin only.
dosing: Adults and children 9 months of age and older: Apply a small amount (about the size of a pea) to the affected skin area twice daily (morning and evening) for 5 days. Only use it for the full 5 days as directed by your doctor, even if the skin looks better sooner.
missed_dose: If you forget to apply a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply extra ointment to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store the ointment at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat and direct sunlight. Keep the tube tightly closed when not in use. Keep this medicine out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Do not use this ointment on your eyes, inside your nose, in your mouth, or on your lips. Avoid getting the ointment near open flames, as it is flammable. Do not use more than the prescribed amount. Do not share this medicine with others, even if they have similar skin problems.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice: signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of your face or throat, or difficulty breathing; your skin infection is getting worse or is not improving after a few days of treatment; severe skin irritation, redness, burning, or swelling at the treated area; or new blisters, peeling, or open sores appear on the treated skin.
when_it_works: You should start to see improvement in your skin infection within a few days of starting treatment. Most people see significant improvement by the end of the 5-day treatment. If your skin does not look better after 3 to 4 days, contact your doctor.
special_populations: Children under 9 months of age should NOT use this medicine, as it has not been proven safe or effective for this age group. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before using this ointment. Elderly patients can generally use this medicine safely, but always follow your doctor's instructions. If you have a weakened immune system or a large area of infected skin, talk to your doctor, as a stronger or different antibiotic may be needed.
